title: China Is Building a Global Infrastructure for Its Cultural Industries
gist: Shanghai's Lingang New Area launched an AI+micro-drama overseas service station on September 4 with service points in Saudi Arabia, Singapore, the UK and Switzerland, integrating the full export chain for Chinese cultural content; online literature, games and micro-dramas are now branded the 'New Three' of Chinese cultural exports.

insights.claim: On September 4, Shanghai's Lingang New Area launched an AI+micro-drama overseas service station with initial service points in Saudi Arabia, Singapore, the United Kingdom and Switzerland.
insights.speaker: Leonie Spangenberg
insights.so_what: Signals state-backed support for Chinese short-video content firms expanding into Gulf, Asian and European markets.

insights.claim: The Lingang service station covers the full export chain for Chinese micro-dramas, including content development, production, translation, distribution, regulatory navigation and localization, rather than merely selling finished products abroad.
insights.speaker: Leonie Spangenberg
insights.so_what: Vertically integrated state export infrastructure lowers barriers for Chinese content platforms, increasing competition for global streaming and short-video incumbents.
insights.quote: Rather than simply helping companies sell finished dramas abroad, it brings several stages of the export process into one system.
insights.locator: The service station covers the full export chain

insights.claim: Online literature, games and micro-dramas are increasingly described in China as the 'New Three' of cultural exports, because all three can be adapted, translated and distributed through digital platforms.
insights.speaker: Leonie Spangenberg
insights.so_what: Watch Chinese gaming, web-fiction and short-drama platforms as a policy-favored export cluster, especially where AI translation cuts localization costs.

insights.claim: Digital adaptability makes the 'New Three' cultural products simpler to take overseas than traditional cultural exports, which is why China is building dedicated global infrastructure around them.
insights.speaker: Leonie Spangenberg
insights.so_what: AI-driven localization is a structural tailwind for Chinese soft-power content and for the platforms distributing it abroad.
